focus: End-focus (new information last) · end-weight (heavy elements last) · fronting for theme and contrast · existential 'there' + inversion · tonic stress placement to steer meaning
focus_ar: التركيز النهائي (الجديد في الآخر)، والثقل النهائي (العناصر الثقيلة في الآخر)، والتقديم للموضوع والمقابلة، و'there' الوجودية مع القلب، وموضع النبر النووي لتوجيه المعنى
arabic_challenge: English organises every sentence around two principles: known information first, new information last (end-focus), and short elements before long ones (end-weight). The tonic stress then lands on that final new element. This is why 'To the committee I gave the report' and 'I gave the report to the committee' say different things. Learners who order clauses by translation rather than by information flow produce sentences that are grammatical but subtly misleading, because the stress lands on something the listener already knew. Arabic word order is flexible in different ways, so the specific English pairing of position with informational status must be learned consciously.

target_sounds: end-focus: new information takes the final tonic stress

isolation.instructions: Put what is NEW at the end, and let the tonic stress fall there naturally. 'I gave the report to the COMMITTEE' answers 'who did you give it to?'. 'I gave the committee the REPORT' answers 'what did you give them?'. Choose the order that puts your news last.
isolation.instructions_ar: ضع الجديد في النهاية ودع النبر النووي يقع هناك طبيعيًا. اختر الترتيب الذي يجعل خبرك في الآخر.

daily_drills.record_this: I gave the report to the committee, not to the board, which is what caused the confusion. She sent me a long letter that same week, and I still have it somewhere. We offered them a modest discount in the end, and to my surprise they accepted immediately.
daily_drills.self_check: Say both orders of the report sentence. Does the tonic stress land on genuinely new information each time?

target_sounds: end-weight: long and heavy elements go last

isolation.instructions: English puts short before long. 'She explained to us the reasons behind the delay' is better than 'She explained the reasons behind the delay to us', because the heavy phrase belongs at the end. Say both and notice how the second stumbles in the middle while the first flows to a clean landing.
isolation.instructions_ar: الإنجليزية تضع القصير قبل الطويل. العبارة الثقيلة تنتمي للنهاية. قل الصيغتين ولاحظ كيف تتعثّر الثانية في الوسط.

sentence_practice: She explained to us the reasons behind the delay.

daily_drills.record_this: She explained to us at some length the reasons behind the unexpected delay. He handed over all the documents he had painstakingly collected that year. They presented to the committee a completely revised plan, which nobody had expected.
daily_drills.self_check: Say the 'explained' sentence both ways. Does putting the heavy phrase last give a cleaner landing?

isolation.instructions: Front an element to make it the topic or to contrast it: 'The first draft I rewrote entirely; the second I left alone.' The fronted element takes a beat plus a small pause, then the clause continues normally. This is how English signals 'as for this one…' without saying it.
isolation.instructions_ar: قدّم عنصرًا لتجعله الموضوع أو للمقابلة. العنصر المُقدَّم يأخذ نبضة ووقفة صغيرة ثم تكمل الجملة عاديًا. هكذا تقول الإنجليزية 'أما هذا…' دون أن تقولها.

daily_drills.self_check: Say the draft sentence. Does each fronted element get a beat and a small pause, with the two halves balanced?

isolation.instructions: 'There' introduces something new into the discourse: 'There remains one difficulty.' 'There followed a long silence.' 'There' itself is completely unstressed /ðə/, the verb is light, and the new noun takes the tonic stress. It exists precisely to delay the news to the end.
isolation.instructions_ar: 'There' تُدخل شيئًا جديدًا في الخطاب. 'There' نفسها غير منبورة تمامًا والفعل خفيف والاسم الجديد يأخذ النبر النووي. وهي موجودة لتأخير الخبر إلى النهاية.

sentence_practice: There remains one difficulty we have not addressed.
There followed a long and uncomfortable silence.
There exists no record of the original agreement.
daily_drills.record_this: There remains one significant difficulty that we have not yet addressed at all. There followed a long and distinctly uncomfortable silence around the table. There exists no written record of the original agreement, which is itself revealing.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'There remains one difficulty'. Is 'there' completely unstressed, with the tonic on 'difficulty'?

target_sounds: moving the tonic stress to steer meaning

isolation.instructions: At mastery level you can leave the words untouched and change the message by moving the tonic stress alone. 'I didn't tell HER' (I told someone else) versus 'I didn't TELL her' (I hinted) versus 'I DIDN'T tell her' (flat denial). Practise all three deliberately and hear each meaning appear.
isolation.instructions_ar: في مستوى الإتقان يمكنك ترك الكلمات كما هي وتغيير الرسالة بنقل النبر النووي فقط. تدرّب على الثلاثة عن قصد واسمع ظهور كل معنى.

sentence_practice: I didn't tell her — I told her assistant.
We can't do it today, but tomorrow is fine.
She said she'd come; she didn't say when.
daily_drills.record_this: I didn't tell her anything at all; I told her assistant, which is quite different. We can't do it today because of the audit, but tomorrow is perfectly fine. She said she would come; she didn't say when, and nobody thought to ask.
daily_drills.self_check: Say 'I didn't tell her' three times, moving the tonic. Do all three versions mean genuinely different things?

challenge_sentences: She explained to us the reasons for the change.
The first half I enjoyed; the second I did not.
There remains one question nobody has asked.
I didn't promise that — I said I would try.
daily_drills.record_this: She explained to us in some detail the reasons behind the sudden change. The first half of the concert I genuinely enjoyed; the second I did not. There remains one obvious question that nobody in the room has asked. I didn't promise that at any point; I said only that I would try.
daily_drills.self_check: Three checks: new information last, heavy elements last, and unstressed 'there' with the tonic on the new noun.

test_yourself.instructions: Record yourself reading this as a considered explanation. Information packaging is invisible when done well, so listen for whether each sentence lands on genuinely new information — then check.
test_yourself.instructions_ar: سجّل نفسك تقرأ هذا كتفسير متأنٍّ. تعبئة المعلومة غير مرئية عند إتقانها، فاستمع هل تهبط كل جملة على معلومة جديدة فعلًا، ثم راجع.
test_yourself.passage: Let me set out what happened, in order. There arose, early in the spring, a disagreement about the budget. I explained to the committee at some length the reasons for the revised figures. The figures themselves nobody disputed; the interpretation they questioned immediately. There followed several weeks of correspondence, most of it unhelpful. I sent the chair a summary; I sent the members the full appendix. That distinction mattered more than it should have. There remains, even now, some confusion about who approved what. As for the timing, I accept responsibility entirely. The delay I could have prevented; the disagreement I could not. There exists no version of these events in which everyone emerges satisfied. Only later did I understand that the argument was never really about money at all.

sounds_to_check.end-focus, tonic on new information: I sent the chair a SUMmary; I sent the members the full apPENdix
sounds_to_check.end-weight, heavy element last: I explained to the committee at some length the reasons for the revised figures
sounds_to_check.fronting for theme and contrast: The figures themselves nobody disputed; the interpretation they questioned · The delay I could have prevented; the disagreement I could not
sounds_to_check.unstressed existential 'there': There arose…, There followed…, There remains…, There exists no version…
sounds_to_check.deliberate tonic placement: the argument was never really about MONey at all

scoring_guide.90_100: Information flows naturally, tonic lands on new material, heavy phrases last, contrasts balanced. Effortless clarity. Ready for week 5.
scoring_guide.70_89: Good; occasionally the tonic lands on known information or a heavy phrase sits mid-sentence.
scoring_guide.50_69: Order follows translation rather than information flow, so stress lands oddly. Repeat days 1-2.
scoring_guide.below_50: Redo days 1-5. Start with end-focus: decide what your news is, then put it last.

for_arabic_speakers: Two rules govern English word order: known before new (end-focus) and short before long (end-weight).
The tonic stress falls on the last new element. If it lands on something the listener already knew, your order is wrong.
Fronting makes something the topic, and needs a beat plus a small pause to work.
Existential 'there' is completely unstressed /ðə/. Stressed 'THERE' means a place instead.
Moving the tonic changes the message without changing a single word. This is one of the clearest markers of mastery.
supplementary_notes.recording_requirement: Record the 'record_this' line daily; on day 7 check that every sentence lands on genuinely new information.
